tasks.short: Review warehouse designs, code and documentation

steps.what: Retrieve the exact design, code, test plan and documentation versions under review
Check explicit code conventions and document completeness requirements
Review designs, codes and test plans for substantive quality and coverage
Write actionable review findings against the relevant artefact versions

loop.purpose: Express the reviewer's actual findings clearly with exact artefact references
loop.input: review judgements and referenced code or document passages
loop.check: Reviewer checks that each comment describes a real defect, points to the correct version and requests a justified change rather than inventing requirements
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; uncertain defects are written manually or omitted
loop.why_not_simpler: The explanation of a design or test-coverage defect is case-specific prose

steps.what: Discuss disputed review findings with the artefact author

tasks.design: Use native versioned review views and configured mechanical checks in {DATA_PLATFORM}. The specialist retains substantive design and test-coverage review, then uses a bounded draft for the actual review comments and discusses disputed findings separately.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mechanical checks and repeated comment composition compete with substantive review.
tasks.enabler_now: Native repository checks can apply explicit conventions, while bounded drafting can express supplied findings.
tasks.still_hard: A design can pass every mechanical check and still implement the wrong data meaning.
tasks.human_edge: Detecting semantic errors and inadequate evidence of business correctness.
tasks.altitude: More attention to semantics, with the same review responsibility.

reach.task: Assess whether a warehouse change preserves the intended data model

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot supplies review assistance and expects oversight; it does not establish correctness of warehouse changes.
Native mechanical checks, reviewer-comment drafting and all time estimates are model knowledge designs.

assumptions: Boundary is an existing peer review and its actual findings record, not authoring or deploying the reviewed change. The specialist is the reviewer, not the author approving their own work. No release or automated comment send is introduced.

The author supplies versioned artefacts and requirement references in the normal review request. s1 counts checking revision IDs and selecting the existing review profile, retaining 12 hours. The profile's explicit convention IDs, required sections and tool versions are supplied by existing engineering standards; missing or ambiguous rules remain manual review in s3.

s2 produces candidate mechanical findings for the checked versions, never a quality approval. The reviewer produces substantive findings in s3 and captures and corrects the actual review text in s4's retained 12 hours. Ordinary review-record saving has no extra gate or saving.
Test native repository checks and review templates before custom code. Existing runtime is not human effort; s2 represents today's manual checks of those explicit conventions only.
unknowns: Actual manual mechanical-check and comment-writing time
research_questions: Do configured checks and drafted comments reduce total review effort without reducing semantic defect detection?

already_counted.description: Verify review versions and correct the actual findings record

incremental.description: Maintain check profiles and sample misleading review comments

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=69, gross=31, upkeep=2, net=29. Cautious case: already linked revisions save nothing in s1, unfamiliar conventions retain 16 of 20 mechanical-check hours and sensitive review wording retains 18 of 20 comment hours; all other 45 hours stay. R=94 gives 6 gross minus 2 upkeep =4. High 18 retains more manual checking and comment correction than central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create warehouse test plans, files and scripts

steps.what: Choose test objectives, boundary cases and expected data outcomes
Create the written unit and integration testing plans

loop.purpose: Draft the plan around the specialist's chosen cases and outcomes
loop.input: test design decisions and referenced requirements
loop.output: draft test plan with requirement-to-case links
loop.check: Specialist checks scenario coverage, failure expectations, prerequisites and independence of expected results from the implementation being tested
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; ambiguous expected behaviour returns to manual planning
loop.why_not_simpler: A test-plan template cannot explain environment-specific data behaviour and failure scenarios

steps.what: Create test files containing the selected fixture rows and expected results
Write scripts implementing the planned warehouse tests

loop.purpose: Draft test-script implementations of explicitly chosen assertions
loop.input: test plan, fixture files and existing test interfaces
loop.output: draft test scripts with referenced assertions
loop.check: Specialist checks joins, null and duplicate behaviour, expected failures, fixture isolation and whether tests can fail when the implementation is wrong
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported interfaces or ambiguous assertions return to manual coding
loop.why_not_simpler: Adapting scripts to transformation interfaces requires code reasoning beyond fixture substitution

steps.what: Run the candidate tests in the isolated test environment and inspect failures
Record validation findings and correct the test artefacts

tasks.design: Use existing fixture builders in {DATA_PLATFORM}, with bounded drafts for the written plan in {DOCS} and test scripts. The specialist chooses expected behaviour, checks the scripts, validates them in isolation and separately records corrections; no production deployment or repository merge is implied.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test plans, repetitive fixture rows and script scaffolding must be built around independently chosen expected results.
tasks.enabler_now: Native fixture builders remove repetitive row construction, while bounded drafting can adapt plan prose and existing test code.
tasks.still_hard: A test can reproduce the implementation's mistake if its expected result is not independent.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing meaningful cases and proving that the tests detect the intended failures.

ambition.what: Evaluate a wider set of null and duplicate scenarios during test design; additional coverage is not counted as time saved.

tasks.altitude: Less scaffold writing with unchanged test-design responsibility.

reach.task: Check whether test fixtures cover a schema contract change
reach.learn: Constraint semantics and independent test oracles

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot provides coding assistance with oversight; its availability does not validate warehouse test assertions.
Native fixture building, bounded plan and script drafts and the time estimates are model knowledge designs.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual plan writing, fixture files, scripts, isolated validation and the existing validation record. Operational execution of the resulting test suite on future releases is separate work. No added merge or approval stage is invented for ordinary author saves.

The specialist produces case ID, input rows, types, null and duplicate cases, expected outputs and expected failures in s1. s3 retains 10 hours to capture and check fixture parameters against the schema, using manual row creation where the builder cannot express a case.

s4 retains 13.75 hours for code inspection and corrections. s5 counts all validation and confirms exact scripts, fixture versions, isolated connection and permitted writes before running. Missing isolation or uncertain side effects prevent execution and require manual correction; no generated pass flag establishes validity.
Test native fixture builders and existing test templates before custom code. Only the bounded draft needs a model; existing test-run runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Fixture-builder coverage and available test components
Actual correction time for generated test code
research_questions: Do drafted tests detect deliberately seeded wrong joins, null handling and duplicate behaviour while reducing total authoring effort?

already_counted.description: Correct the plan, verify fixtures and scripts, validate and record findings

incremental.description: Maintain fixture helpers and sample weak generated assertions

approvals.approved_version: Exact test-script and fixture versions, isolated connection and allowed writes checked before the validation run in s5; any change invalidates run approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=70.75, gross=29.25, upkeep=2, net=27.25. Cautious case: novel integration behaviour retains 19 of 20 plan hours, unsupported fixture shapes retain 18 of 20 fixture hours and unfamiliar test interfaces retain 23 of 25 script hours; other 35 hours stay. R=95 gives 5 gross minus 2 upkeep =3. High 17 retains more script correction and fixture work than central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select warehouse evaluation methods and criteria

steps.what: Clarify the warehouse outcomes and evaluation constraints with stakeholders
Review existing methods, techniques and evidence about their applicability
Select methods, techniques and criteria that fit the evaluative purpose
Write the chosen evaluation criteria, rationale and limits

loop.purpose: Express the selected criteria and their rationale clearly
loop.input: specialist's method decisions and checked references
loop.output: draft criteria record with definitions and limits
loop.check: Specialist checks that metric definitions, thresholds, population and caveats represent the actual decisions and do not create unsupported standards
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; undefined criteria return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: The rationale and limitations depend on the warehouse's evaluation purpose

steps.what: Explain the selected criteria and trade-offs to warehouse stakeholders

tasks.design: Use native reference search and a criteria-record template in {DOCS}. Keep method selection with the specialist and draft only the written rationale, separately from stakeholder discussions; no automated ranking or acceptance decision is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rationale for selected criteria must be rebuilt from reference material after the decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Native search and bounded prose drafting can reduce retrieval and recording effort.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing criteria that measure business correctness rather than convenient technical proxies.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising the trade-off between a measurable property and the outcome stakeholders need.
tasks.altitude: Less supporting prose, with the same evaluation-method decisions.

reach.task: Assess whether an evaluation criterion reflects the intended warehouse contract

evidence.claim: Native method-reference search and bounded criteria-rationale drafting are model knowledge designs with no task-specific measured digest case.

assumptions: Boundary includes stakeholder clarification, reference review, method selection, its actual written criteria record and explanation. Running evaluations and accepting releases are separate work and receive no saving here.

Stakeholders supply outcome, population and constraints in s1, with all conversation time retained. The specialist produces method, metric definition, population, threshold if justified, rationale and limits in s3 and captures and corrects those fields in s4's retained 13 hours. No free structured acceptance criterion is assumed from a meeting.

Missing definitions or unsupported thresholds require manual clarification and writing. Test native references and criteria templates first. Ordinary author saves have no approval stage or saving, and the model has no authority to select methods.
unknowns: Availability of reusable criteria and references
Actual time spent recording method-selection rationale
research_questions: Does drafting preserve the specialist's chosen metric meaning and limitations while reducing correction-inclusive writing time?

already_counted.description: Verify method references and correct the criteria record

incremental.description: Maintain reference links and sample criteria-definition drift

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=90, gross=10, upkeep=1, net=9. Cautious case: a new evaluation purpose retains all 20 reference hours and 19 of 20 rationale-writing hours; other 60 hours remain, giving 1 gross minus 1 upkeep =0. High 5 retains more metric-definition correction than central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify the business rule, exceptions and affected warehouse interfaces
Write the implementation specification and concrete expected examples
Implement business rules in stored procedures or middleware code

loop.purpose: Draft implementation code for explicitly specified rule behaviour
loop.input: checked rule specification, concrete examples and existing interfaces
loop.check: Specialist checks joins, transaction behaviour, nulls, duplicates, error paths and fidelity to the specified business rule before testing
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; ambiguous behaviour or unsupported interfaces return to manual coding
loop.why_not_simpler: Integrating a rule into existing procedures requires code reasoning beyond substituting configuration fields

steps.what: Test the implementation against expected examples and integration effects
Review the final implementation and its test evidence for release
Deploy the exact reviewed rule change through the existing release process

tasks.design: Use a native rule-specification template in {DOCS} and bounded code drafting in {DATA_PLATFORM}, checking native configuration before writing procedures. Testing, existing peer review and the separate release action remain fully retained; the model cannot deploy its draft.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rule details and implementation scaffolding must be written around clarified business behaviour.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates remove repeated specification layout, and code assistance can draft implementation around explicit examples.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous business meaning, transaction side effects and effects on downstream consumers.
tasks.human_edge: Translating a business promise into correct data behaviour and validating it independently.
tasks.altitude: Less implementation typing, with unchanged rule and release accountability.

reach.task: Assess a rule change's effect on downstream data contracts

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot provides coding assistance with oversight; that capability does not remove warehouse testing or release review.
Specification templates, bounded rule implementation and the estimated time benefits are model knowledge designs.

assumptions: Boundary includes rule clarification, its actual written specification, implementation, testing, existing independent peer review and deployment. The modeled team already uses peer-reviewed releases; no new approval layer or saving in reviewer time is claimed. The reviewer is a different person from the author.

The business owner supplies intended rule behaviour and exceptions in s1. The specialist produces input fields, predicates, output fields, null and duplicate treatment, failure behaviour and expected examples in s2, retaining 10.5 baseline workflow hours for actual capture and verification. Missing semantics require manual clarification rather than generated defaults.

The specialist checks drafted code in s3 and runs it only in the isolated test environment in s4, with all testing time retained. Existing tests are inputs; new test artefact creation is separately task 16130 and is not double-counted as a saving here. The reviewed change package binds code version, configuration, test results and release target.

Try native warehouse rule configuration before code drafting. Ordinary source saves have no self-approval or saving. s6 is a real deployment, not a file save, and keeps its full small time. Outside reviewer time remains outside the focal denominator; no effort transfer is credited.
research_questions: Does assisted implementation reduce total specification and code effort after all test and review corrections?

already_counted.description: Capture the rule specification, inspect drafted code and test implementation behaviour
Existing independent release review stays fully retained

incremental.description: Maintain specification templates and sample generated rule defects

approvals.approved_version: Exact implementation version, test data and isolated test connection checked before testing in s4; changed code or connection requires renewed checking
Exact implementation and configuration versions, release target and test evidence reviewed by the independent reviewer in s5; any change voids release approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: focal B=90, R=72, gross=20%, incremental focal upkeep=2 per 100 focal hours, net=18%. Reviewer share 10 stays outside B. Cautious case: complex rule details retain 14.3 of 15 specification hours and unfamiliar middleware retains 28 of 30 coding hours; other focal 45 hours stay. R=87.3 gives 3% gross minus 2 upkeep =1. High 11 retains more implementation correction than central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The specialist keeps warehouse semantics, test design and operational responsibility while reducing selected drafting and mechanical checks.
reach: Work with database architects to validate rule and schema contracts
role.ambitious_version: Better evidenced warehouse changes and broader test scenarios within existing human release controls.
